handback.t:
d5 is built and run on both seed sets. In this synthetic world the router raises graded quality over static keywords when the keyword map is wrong, stale or trapped. With an honest map the gain is small, and warm(hebr) is worse than keyword early.

**Where the router helps (held-out 31-60)**
- In misleading-keywords, drift and noisy+failing, warm and the retuned guarded router gain about +.05 to +.085 over keyword (e.g. .554 to .638 in misleading-keywords). That closes roughly 40-70% of the keyword-to-oracle gap.
- Retuned guarded(hebr) does this without the early cost. It equals keyword at the first 100 and 250 tasks, and beats keyword at first250 in misleading-keywords (+.027) and noisy+failing (+.015).

**Where it doesn't**
- With an honest keyword map (clear-specialists, many-generalists) the gain is only about +.005 to +.015.
- warm(hebr) loses to keyword at first100 in all 7 worlds (-.008 to -.094, Holm-significant), and the same losses appear on 61-90.
- The x1-frozen guarded config does not carry over. Against warm it loses -.040 in drift (last500 -.124), -.025 in noisy+failing, and -.024 in misleading-keywords, on both seed sets.
- The retuned guarded config beats warm in clear-specialists and misleading-keywords, but still loses to warm in drift at last500 (-.020).
- In the control world, where all agents are about equal, every learner is slightly below keyword (warm -.007), so nothing is gained there. There are no false-positive wins.
- No domain wins on its own. Per-domain effects follow the world-level sign. The one exception is misleading-keywords, where guarded-x1 loses to warm in debugging alone (-.033, -.038 on 61-90). That is consistent with the language decoy keyword, but I did not isolate it.
- eps-greedy is the strongest plain learner late. At last500 it beats the keyword-prior routers in noisy+failing and mixed-domain.

**World and protocol**
- 4 domains x 4 sub-skills, 8 hidden agents, and 7 world variants: clear-specialists, many-generalists, misleading-keywords, drift, noisy+failing, mixed-domain, and a near-equal control.
- Quality is graded in [0,1] (reward to routers is realized quality). The reported metric is the mean expected quality of the chosen agent, against the oracle best agent per task.
- eps-greedy, pooled-thompson and a guarded retune were tuned on seeds 1-8. Held-out 31-60 and confirmation 61-90 use the same frozen configs.
- Paired t 95% CIs against the best fair baseline per world and window, with Holm over 84 tests. The per-domain family is Holm-corrected separately.

**Caveats**
- The world is fully synthetic. Skills, noise, decoy rates and drift size are my choices, and there is only one drift type.
- The retuned guarded config was tuned on this world family, so its wins are optimistic. The x1-frozen config is the out-of-family test, and it fails 3 of 7 worlds.
- In the board section I added an untested hypothesis for why the x1 guard stalls after drift: pooled features may keep the stale agent's confidence bound high.

I made no src edits and installed nothing. Each run takes about 6 seconds. The exact rerun commands with the PATH/CARGO_TARGET_DIR exports are in the board entry "VERIFY REQUEST — CODE-QUALITY — d5 task-quality world", which I appended to `results/research_board.md`. It also has the per-world table, diffs with CIs, win/loss lists and the full caveats.
